concepts: ore of aluminium - bauxite vs cryolite
questions.question: The ore of Aluminium is:
questions.solution: (d) Cryolite (as printed in the paper's key; strictly bauxite is the chief ore of aluminium, but cryolite is the only aluminium-containing option)

questions.question: Hydrogen chloride gas is not collected over water, as:

options.a: It is highly soluble in water.
options.b: It is less soluble in water.

questions.solution: (a) It is highly soluble in water.

questions.question: An aqueous solution of ammonia is:
questions.solution: (c) Basic

concepts: basic oxide + acid gives salt and water
questions.question: The metallic oxide which when reacts with HCl forms salt and water:
questions.solution: (d) Sodium oxide: a metallic oxide that reacts with HCl to give salt and water (Na2O + 2HCl -> 2NaCl + H2O). (The printed key shows (c) ammonium hydroxide, which is not an oxide: a printing error.)

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: Define: Isomerism
questions.solution: Isomerism: substances having the same molecular formula but different structural formulae (and hence different physical and chemical properties) are called isomers; the phenomenon is isomerism.

marking_points.point: Same molecular formula but different structural formulae (different properties)

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
concepts: excess NH3 with Cl2 gives NH4Cl
questions.question: State a compound formed when excess ammonia gas reacts with chlorine.
questions.solution: Printed key: nitrogen trichloride (NCl3) with HCl, NH3 + Cl2 -> NCl3 + 3HCl. Chemically, with excess ammonia the products are ammonium chloride and nitrogen (8NH3 + 3Cl2 -> 6NH4Cl + N2); NCl3 forms with excess chlorine. Accept ammonium chloride (NH4Cl)/nitrogen or the printed nitrogen trichloride (NCl3).

marking_points.point: Ammonium chloride (NH4Cl) / nitrogen, or printed answer nitrogen trichloride (NCl3)

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B

concepts: Contact process - oleum diluted with water
questions.question: State a substance added to water, to manufacture sulphuric acid in Contact process.
questions.solution: Oleum (H2S2O7, fuming sulphuric acid): SO3 is absorbed in conc. H2SO4 to form oleum, which is then diluted with water to give sulphuric acid. (Catalyst used in the process is vanadium pentoxide.)

marking_points.point: Oleum (H2S2O7), added to water

questions.solution: P is carbon dioxide (CO2), formed when a metal carbonate or bicarbonate reacts with an acid.

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: State the observation: Dry ammonia gas reacts with oxygen in the presence of a catalyst.
questions.solution: Ammonia is oxidised in presence of platinum catalyst to nitric oxide and water vapour (heat evolved): 4NH3 + 5O2 -> 4NO + 6H2O. Nitric oxide turns reddish-brown on contact with air.

marking_points.point: Nitric oxide (NO) and water vapour (steam) form in presence of platinum catalyst

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
concepts: ammonia with chlorine - dense white fumes of NH4Cl
questions.question: State the observation: Excess ammonia gas reacts with chlorine.
questions.solution: Printed key: a vigorous reaction producing nitrogen trichloride and hydrochloric acid, NH3 + Cl2 -> NCl3 + 3HCl. Chemically, excess ammonia gives dense white fumes of ammonium chloride (and nitrogen gas): 8NH3 + 3Cl2 -> 6NH4Cl + N2. Accept either.

marking_points.point: Dense white fumes of ammonium chloride (nitrogen evolved); or printed: vigorous reaction forming NCl3 and HCl

marking_points.point: Reddish-brown fumes of NO2 evolved (with CO2 and water)

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
concepts: Baeyer's process - bauxite dissolves in NaOH, amphoteric alumina
questions.question: State the relevant reason: Concentrated alkali is used for the concentration of bauxite ore.
questions.solution: Bauxite (alumina) dissolves in hot concentrated sodium hydroxide solution (forming sodium aluminate) while impurities (iron oxide, silica etc.) remain insoluble and are filtered out. This process is called leaching (Baeyer's process).

marking_points.point: Alumina dissolves in hot conc. NaOH (as sodium aluminate) while impurities are insoluble and are filtered off

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
concepts: reduction of alumina by electrolysis - reactive metal
questions.question: State the relevant reason: Fused alumina is reduced to aluminium by electrolysis.
questions.solution: Alumina is highly stable, so it cannot be reduced by chemical reducing agents like carbon; aluminium is a strong reducing metal, so electrolytic reduction is used. Al is obtained at the cathode, oxygen at the anode. Ionisation: Al2O3 -> 2Al3+ + 3O2-.

marking_points.point: Alumina is very stable / aluminium is highly reactive so cannot be reduced by chemical reducing agents; electrolysis is needed

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: State one use of the alloy Magnalium.
questions.solution: Magnalium (Al + Mg) is light and strong; used in making light instruments, balance beams and aircraft/scientific instrument parts. (Part marked out of syllabus; no printed answer in the key.)

marking_points.point: One correct use, e.g. making light instruments, balance beams, aircraft parts

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: State one use of the alloy Duralumin.
questions.solution: Duralumin (aluminium and copper with Mg, Mn): used in making parts for aircraft, trucks, rivets, etc.

marking_points.point: One correct use: aircraft parts / trucks / rivets / utensils

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
concepts: sulphite gives SO2 with dilute acid
questions.question: Distinguish between sodium sulphite solution and sodium sulphate solution using dilute H2SO4.
questions.solution: Sodium sulphite with dil. H2SO4 gives effervescence of colourless gas SO2 with suffocating smell, which turns acidified potassium dichromate paper green: Na2SO3 + H2SO4 -> Na2SO4 + H2O + SO2. Sodium sulphate gives no reaction (no gas).

marking_points.point: Sodium sulphite: effervescence of SO2 (choking smell, turns acidified K2Cr2O7 green)
Sodium sulphate: no reaction / no gas evolved

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Lead vs zinc salt with NH4OH
concepts: Pb2+ vs Zn2+ with excess NH4OH
questions.question: Distinguish between lead salt solution and zinc salt solution using NH4OH solution in excess.
questions.solution: Lead salt: white precipitate of Pb(OH)2 which is insoluble in excess NH4OH. Zinc salt: white (gelatinous) precipitate of Zn(OH)2 which dissolves in excess NH4OH giving a colourless solution. (Printed key says zinc gives a gelatinous white precipitate; the precipitate is soluble in excess, which is the distinguishing feature.)

marking_points.point: Lead salt: white precipitate insoluble in excess NH4OH
Zinc salt: white precipitate soluble in excess NH4OH

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
concepts: HCl with lead nitrate gives PbCl2 soluble on heating
